assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt the thin base_floor plate to the ground plane; it is the root structural member and all other modules ultimately connect to it.
2. Install front_rail, rear_rail, left_rail, and right_rail on top of base_floor to mark the footprint of the open architecture frame.

3. Fasten post_front_left, post_front_right, post_back_left, and post_back_right to the rails, then attach top_bridge, top_rear_bridge, top_left_bridge, and top_right_bridge as perimeter rails rather than a roof.
4. Mount input_text_plate and embedding_table on the center front rail; text tokens enter the embedding table before rising through the residual spine.
5. Mount input_image_plate, pan_scan_turntable, siglip_encoder, crop_token_tiles, and vision_text_projector on the left branch, then connect the projector into embedding_table.
6. Install residual_pipe vertically through the open frame and connect embedding_table to it as the main inference data path.
7. Slide local_band_01 through local_band_10 and global_band_01 through global_band_02 onto the residual_pipe in the visible 5-local-to-1-global rhythm.

8. Bolt schedule_cartridge_01 through schedule_cartridge_12 to the rear-left service side; each cartridge represents one compact 5L+1G repeat, with the final cartridge noting the truncated 62-layer tail.
9. Attach layer_ruler_spine and the grouped 62_notch rail to the right service side so the total layer count is mechanically countable while the main stack remains open.

10. Attach the canonical exploded transformer cell around layer_window_slot: pre-attention norm, QKV projection, QK-Norm, RoPE, attention kernel, O-projection, attention post-norm, FFN pre-norm, SwiGLU FFN, and FFN post-norm.

11. Bolt kv_cache_window_column and kv_cache_global_column to the left service rail and connect both to attention_kernel to show the cheap local window cache and the smaller set of full-context global caches.
12. Mount prediction_head at the top of residual_pipe, then route student_logits_conduit from the head to loss_node.
13. Ground teacher_model, optimizer_adamw, training_data_pipe, and parallelism_plan on their own pedestals or rails.

14. Route teacher_logits_conduit into loss_node, loss_gradient_conduit from loss_node to optimizer_adamw, adamw_update_conduit from optimizer_adamw back to residual_pipe, and data_ingest_conduit from training_data_pipe to embedding_table.

info.summary: 27B-parameter DENSE decoder-only multimodal LM from Google DeepMind. 62 layers × 5376 hidden dim, 32 query heads / 16 KV heads (GQA, ratio 2), SwiGLU FFN, dual RMSNorm (pre + post) on every sublayer, QK-Norm, and the signature 5:1 LOCAL-to-GLOBAL attention pattern (sliding-window 1024 + full-context). Vision through a frozen SigLIP-400M encoder with Pan-and-Scan, 896×896 crops, 256 soft-tokens per image. 128K context (32K for the 1B variant), trained on ~14T tokens with knowledge distillation from a larger teacher.
info.description:
Gemma 3 is the third generation of Google's open Gemma family. Compared with Gemma 2 it (i) goes multimodal via SigLIP + Pan&Scan, (ii) extends context 8K → 128K, (iii) replaces attention soft-cap with QK-Norm, (iv) uses an extreme 5:1 ratio of LOCAL (sliding-window) to GLOBAL attention layers — local layers do almost all the work, global layers carry long-range information. Local layers use RoPE base 10,000 (standard); global layers use RoPE base 1,000,000 to keep extrapolation clean to 128K. Both pre-norm AND post-norm RMSNorm are applied to attention and FFN — empirically improves training stability of fp16/bf16 deep stacks. The model is DENSE (no MoE) — every parameter activates for every token. Trained on ~14 T tokens via large-batch SGD with knowledge distillation from a larger Gemini teacher.

Design rationale, in one line each:
• 5:1 local:global: makes long-context KV cheap because 5/6 of layers only need a 1024-token window.
• QK-Norm: removes attention-logit blow-ups at long context without the soft-cap's training instability.
• Dual norm (pre+post): cheap stability win for very deep stacks.
• SigLIP + Pan&Scan: handles non-square / high-resolution images without resize artefacts.
• Distillation from teacher: smaller models inherit teacher knowledge cheaply.

comparisons.delta: Gemma 2 was text-only with 8K context, alternating local-global attention at a milder ratio (1:1), used attention soft-cap (logit clipping) for stability, and pre-norm only. Gemma 3 keeps the dense architecture but adds vision (SigLIP + Pan&Scan), extends context to 128K, swaps soft-cap for QK-Norm, pushes the local:global ratio to 5:1 (massive KV win), and adds post-norm RMSNorm. Vocab 256K stays.

Gemma 1 was vanilla text-only LLaMA-style: pre-norm RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU, MHA. Gemma 3 keeps the surface but replaces literally every attention block with a 5:1 local-global GQA + QK-Norm + dual-norm hybrid, adds multimodal input via SigLIP, jumps from 8K to 128K context, uses distillation from a larger teacher, and is much wider/deeper at the 27B point.

LLaMA-3 70B and Mistral-Large are GQA dense decoders with full-context attention and standard pre-norm. Gemma 3 trades width/depth for a smarter attention plan — 5/6 of its layers are local (1024-token window) so its KV cache is 5–10× smaller at 128K context for similar quality. It is also natively multimodal where most peers bolt vision on as a separate model.

Gemma 3 is fundamentally different: DENSE (every parameter active for every token) where V3/GLM are sparse MoE. Trade-off: at 27B Gemma 3 activates 27B per token (vs ~32B for GLM-4.5 at 355B total), so Gemma 3 hits more compute per token relative to capacity. Gemma 3 has no expert all-to-all bottleneck — single-node inference is dramatically simpler. It's also smaller in absolute capacity but matches MoE peers up to its size class because of the strong attention plan and distillation.

parts.name: Right Compute Rail
parts.role: Right rail supports the exploded FFN side and the 62-notch layer ruler.

parts.name: Front Right Open-Frame Post
parts.role: Vertical post that makes the tower readable as a built assembly rather than a stack of floating blocks.

parts.name: Back Left Open-Frame Post
parts.role: Rear post that braces the left service side while preserving X-ray visibility through the frame.

parts.name: Back Right Open-Frame Post
parts.role: Rear post that braces the compute side and gives the model a clear mechanical assembly boundary.

parts.name: Top Front Bridge Rail
parts.role: Front upper rail ties the two front posts while leaving the prediction head visible from above and ISO.

parts.name: Top Rear Bridge Rail
parts.role: Rear upper rail completes the open top frame without making an opaque roof.

parts.name: Top Left Side Rail
parts.role: Left upper rail braces the cache and vision side while keeping the transformer interior exposed.

parts.name: Top Right Side Rail
parts.role: Right upper rail braces the FFN side and ruler without covering the stack.

parts.name: Input Tokens Plate
parts.role: Grounded plate where multilingual SentencePiece text tokens with vocabulary size 256K enter the model.

parts.name: Input Image Plate
parts.role: Grounded image input plate for variable-resolution RGB images before Pan-and-Scan cropping.
parts.algorithm: image: H x W x 3 RGB

parts.name: Pan-and-Scan Slicer
parts.role: Rotary slicer symbol showing non-square images split into overlapping 896 by 896 crops before encoding.

parts.name: 896 Crop Tile A
parts.role: First visible 896 by 896 crop emitted by Pan-and-Scan for independent SigLIP processing.

parts.name: 896 Crop Tile B
parts.role: Second visible 896 by 896 crop showing that multiple image windows can feed the same frozen encoder.

parts.name: 896 Crop Tile C
parts.role: Third visible crop tile making the Pan-and-Scan fan-out legible in the isometric render.

parts.name: SigLIP-400M Frozen Vision Encoder
parts.role: Frozen SigLIP ViT encoder that turns each 896 by 896 crop into features for 256 soft tokens.

parts.name: Vision-Text Projector
parts.role: Linear projector maps SigLIP crop features into the LLM hidden dimension d=5376.

parts.name: Embedding Table V=256K d=5376
parts.role: Tied token embedding table that combines text embeddings and projected image soft tokens before the residual stream.
parts.memory_footprint: 256000 x 5376 x BF16 is about 2.75 GiB

parts.name: Residual Stream d=5376
parts.role: Central vertical residual bus carrying hidden state through 62 dense transformer layers.
parts.algorithm: x = x + post_attn(attn(pre_attn(x))); x = x + post_ffn(ffn(pre_ffn(x)))

parts.name: Exploded Canonical Transformer Slot
parts.role: Transparent visual slot that marks one opened transformer layer so its submodules can be inspected around the residual pipe.

parts.name: Local Layer Band 1
parts.role: Visible local attention band representing a sliding-window layer with 1024-token context and RoPE base 10000.

parts.name: Local Layer Band 2
parts.role: Second local band in the 5:1 local-to-global schedule; it caches only a 1024-token window.

parts.name: Local Layer Band 3
parts.role: Third local band showing that most Gemma 3 layers avoid full-context attention cost.

parts.name: Local Layer Band 4
parts.role: Fourth local band in the first visible 5-local group before a global layer appears.

parts.name: Local Layer Band 5
parts.role: Fifth local band completing one local group before the full-context global band.

parts.name: Global Layer Band 6

parts.name: Local Layer Band 7

parts.name: Local Layer Band 8

parts.name: Global Layer Notches 6 12 18 24 30 36 42 48 54 60

parts.name: Layer Notches 31-62 Local Bank
parts.role: Dense upper comb of thirty-two layer notches completes the count through layer 62.

parts.name: Pre-Attention RMSNorm
parts.role: Pre-attention RMSNorm normalizes hidden states before QKV projection using a learned gamma vector of length d.

parts.name: GQA QKV Projection 32Q 16KV
parts.role: Fused projection creates 32 query heads and 16 shared key-value heads for grouped-query attention.

parts.name: QK-Norm Ring
parts.role: Ring symbol for RMSNorm applied to query and key vectors before attention logits are formed.

parts.name: RoPE Dual-Base Ring
parts.role: Ring symbol for RoPE using base 10000 on local layers and base 1000000 on global layers.

parts.name: FlashAttention Kernel
parts.role: Attention compute block applies either a 1024-token sliding mask for local layers or a full causal mask for global layers.
parts.flops_per_token: local about 8 MFLOP; global about 1 GFLOP at T=128K
parts.algorithm: out = flash_attn(Q,K,V, mask = local ? sliding_1024 : causal_full)

parts.name: Attention O Projection
parts.role: Output projection maps the concatenated attention heads back to hidden width d=5376.

parts.name: Post-Attention RMSNorm
parts.role: Post-attention RMSNorm normalizes the attention output before it is added back to the residual stream.

parts.name: Pre-FFN RMSNorm
parts.role: Pre-FFN RMSNorm normalizes the residual stream before the dense SwiGLU feed-forward network.

parts.name: Dense SwiGLU FFN dff=21504
parts.role: Dense SwiGLU feed-forward network with intermediate size 21504; every parameter is active for every token because Gemma 3 is not MoE.
parts.memory_footprint: about 692 MB BF16 per layer for three FFN matrices
parts.algorithm: h = silu(x @ W_gate) * (x @ W_up); y = h @ W_down

parts.name: Post-FFN RMSNorm
parts.role: Post-FFN RMSNorm stabilizes the dense feed-forward output before residual addition.

parts.name: Local Window KV Cache
parts.role: Tall narrow cache column for the five-sixths of layers that only retain a 1024-token sliding window.
parts.memory_footprint: about 200 MB for local layers at 1024-token windows

parts.name: Global KV Cache
parts.role: Slimmer count column for the one-sixth of layers that retain full 128K-context key-value pages.
parts.memory_footprint: about 5 GB for global layers at 128K context with 16 KV heads

parts.name: Tied LM Head V=256K
parts.role: Tied output projection converts final hidden state back into logits over the 256K-token vocabulary.

parts.name: CE plus Distillation Loss
parts.role: Loss node combines next-token cross-entropy with KL distillation from the larger Gemini teacher.

parts.name: Student Logits Conduit
parts.role: Horizontal conduit carrying the Gemma 3 prediction-head logits into the training loss node.

parts.name: Teacher Logits Distillation Conduit
parts.role: Distinct training-only conduit routes soft targets from the larger Gemini teacher into the loss node.

parts.name: Loss Gradient Return Conduit
parts.role: Training-only return line carries the scalar loss and gradients down to the AdamW optimizer block.

parts.name: AdamW Update Conduit
parts.role: Ground-level update line returns AdamW parameter updates from optimizer state back toward the dense model stack.

parts.name: Training Data Ingest Conduit
parts.role: Low grounded conduit feeds the 14T-token training corpus from the data plate into the embedding table.

parts.name: Teacher Model Pedestal
parts.role: Grounded pedestal that prevents the training teacher from floating above the main assembly.

parts.name: Larger Gemini Teacher
parts.role: Frozen larger Gemini model that supplies soft targets for knowledge distillation during training.

parts.name: AdamW Optimizer Block
parts.role: Grounded training optimizer block representing AdamW large-batch updates and two optimizer-state tensors.
parts.memory_footprint: Adam state is about 2 times parameter size

parts.name: 14T Token Data Pipe
parts.role: Grounded data feed plate for roughly 14 trillion multilingual text and image-text training tokens.

parts.name: TP DP FSDP Parallelism Plan
parts.role: Translucent training plan block showing tensor parallelism, data parallelism, and FSDP sharding without expert parallelism because the model is dense.
